Q1: Di-n-octyl phthalate presents known GHS-level hazards for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity (CMR) and inhalation (IHL). An expanded perspective indicates potential endocrine disruption (EDC), environmental (ENV), and dermal/eye (SKN) hazards. While oral exposure (ORL) is associated with low to moderate hazards, information regarding organ and systemic hazards (OGN) is currently data deficient.
Q2: This chemical is listed on several "Lists of Concern." It is identified on The Endocrine Disruption Exchange (TEDX) list as a potential endocrine disruptor, and is also included in the "Substitute In Now" (SINLIST), suggesting it as a candidate for replacement.
Q3: Di-n-octyl phthalate is generally well-characterized, supported by over 7,000 literature references, significantly above the median for characterized chemicals. It has a precisely defined molecular formula (C24H38O4) and is classified as a "Small Molecule," indicating it is not an incompletely defined substance, although there is a deficiency in data for organ and systemic hazards.
